The recurring section of the annual Defense appropriations act that lets the Secretary of Defense, with the approval of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, move funds between accounts up to a cap set each year ($6 billion for fiscal 2026). Transfers must be for higher-priority items based on unforeseen military requirements and may never fund an item Congress has denied.

::: {.official-links}
**Read the law** (official GovInfo text)

[Enacted text: Pub. L. 119-75](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/plaw/119/public/75){.btn-official}
:::

## Key provisions

- A determination by the Secretary that the transfer is necessary in the national interest, and OMB approval.
- An annual dollar cap; transfers among military personnel accounts do not count against it.
- Only for higher-priority items based on unforeseen military requirements, and never where Congress denied the item.
- Prompt notice to Congress of every transfer; requests for multiple reprogrammings due by June 30 of the fiscal year.

## Why it matters

Transfer and reprogramming rules are how the Appropriations Committees keep the money where they put it. The limits matter most in disputes: in 2019 the Defense Department used general transfer authority to move funds into counterdrug accounts for border barrier construction under [Section 284 (counterdrug)](sec284-counterdrug-1990.qmd), alongside emergency construction under [Section 2808 (construction)](sec2808-milcon-1982.qmd), and litigation over whether the barrier was an item Congress had denied followed. The [Antideficiency Act](antideficiency.qmd) and the purpose statute (31 U.S.C. 1301(a)) are the background rules a transfer must still satisfy.

## Current status

Re-enacted each year in the Defense appropriations act; cited here as enacted for fiscal year 2026. A continuing resolution carries it forward on the prior year's terms. Check current status.

[Last checked November 24, 2026.]{.checked}
